item.title: CIA releases dozens of presidential briefings from before and after 9/11
item.description: The CIA has released dozens of previously classified documents tied to 9/11. CBS News intelligence and national security reporter Olivia Gazis has more.

item.title: U.S. inflation rises as Fed considers interest rate
item.description: Inflation in the U.S. is rising yet again, with the Labor Department saying consumer prices in August rose 3.4% year over year. CBS News correspondent Natalie Brand has more.

item.title: Onboard the USS George Washington as it operates in the Middle East
item.description: CBS News national investigative correspondent Tom Hanson reports from aboard the USS George Washington aircraft carrier as it operates in the Middle East.

item.title: 9/11 remembered, 25 years later, in New York, at the Pentagon and in Shanksville, PA
item.description: Ceremonies were held Friday as the United States marked 25 years since the 9/11 terror attacks. CBS News' Jericka Duncan and Nicole Sganga have more.

item.title: Midterms forecast for the House and Senate, as of right now
item.description: Friday marks 53 days until the November midterm elections. Zachary Donnini, head of data science at VoteHub.com, joins "The Takeout" to dive into the numbers and their implications on the battle for the balance of power in Congress.

item.title: CIA declassifies presidential daily briefs leading up to 9/11 attacks
item.description: The CIA on Friday declassified 71 presidential daily briefs dating from February 1998 to Sept. 12, 2001. CBS News national security contributor Samantha Vinograd joins with analysis.

item.title: Work of 9/11 Victim Compensation Fund continues 25 years after attacks
item.description: Since reopening in 2011, the 9/11 Victim Compensation Fund has awarded more than $18 billion to those impacted by the attacks. Its special master, Allison Turkel, joins "The Takeout" to discuss the program's work 25 years after the attacks.

item.title: Rubio told supporters he's not planning on running for president in 2028, sources say
item.description: Sources close to Secretary of State Marco Rubio tell CBS News that he has privately told supporters who have urged him to run for president in 2028 that he is not planning on launching a second White House bid. Dave Levinthal, senior editor at the Washington Sun, and Julia Manchester, White House correspondent for The Hill, join to discuss.

item.title: Trump ties Iran war to 9/11 attacks, war on terror in Pentagon speech
item.description: On Friday morning, at the ceremony of remembrance for the 184 who died at the Pentagon when hijacked American Airlines Flight 77 crashed there on 9/11, President Trump put the Iran war in the context of fighting global terrorism and one of its persistent state sponsors. CBS News chief White House correspondent Nancy Cordes reports.

item.title: Michigan Senate candidates battle over their records on 9/11 at 25-year mark
item.description: The candidates in Michigan's closely watched U.S. Senate race, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers, have exchanged criticism over their records on the 9/11 attacks.

item.title: Major Garrett recalls traveling with Bush on morning of 9/11
item.description: On the morning of Sept. 11, 2001, CBS News chief Washington correspondent Major Garrett was traveling with then-President George W. Bush to cover his visit to a Florida elementary school. Then, the world changed. Garrett recalls the uncertainty of those early hours.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Sept. 13)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Trump admin to send $500 checks to nearly 1 million ACA enrollees
item.description: Affordable Care Act recipients in 30 states are set to receive the $500 checks starting in October. Here's why.

item.title: Ex-CIA official found with $40 million in gold bars in plea deal talks
item.description: The court filing did not indicate what charges David Rush could plead to.

item.title: Daughter of Gary Geidel, firefighter who died on 9/11, shares her memories of that day
item.description: Tillie Geidel Conklin, daughter of FDNY firefighter Gary Geidel, joins CBS News to share her memories of her father and what it was like to lose him on 9/11.

item.title: Daughters of 9/11 victims seek answers about accused mastermind's trial
item.description: A new documentary, "Daughters of 9/11," follows their pursuit of information and closure, which they were determined to find for themselves, other families who lost loved ones in the attacks and the American public.

item.title: Diesel hits record $6 a gallon as Iran-backed Houthis take key Red Sea territory
item.description: The moves by the Houthis make it easier for the Iran-backed rebels to target ships transiting the crucial Bab el-Mandeb Strait for Saudi Arabian oil exports.

item.title: Life in rural Afghanistan, 25 years after 9/11
item.description: Most of the fighting during the nearly 20-year war between the U.S. and the Taliban that followed the 9/11 terrorist attacks was in rural Afghanistan. CBS News senior foreign correspondent Imtiaz Tyab traveled to those provinces to see what life is like there now.

item.title: "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" guests for Sept. 13, 2026
item.description: This week's guests include Republican Utah Gov. Spencer Cox and Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed.

item.title: Lawsuit seeks to block deployment of ICE, federal agents to polling sites
item.description: A coalition of advocacy groups and a Democratic-led city filed a preemptive lawsuit seeking to block the Trump administration from deploying armed ICE agents to polling sites ahead of the midterm elections.

item.title: Doctor on why she was immediately skeptical of Elizabeth Holmes' Theranos claims
item.description: Dr. Courtney Lawrence, a board-certified blood donation and transfusion doctor, shared her thoughts on Elizabeth Holmes' now-defunct company Theranos and its promise to transform complex blood testing. Lawrence shared why she was immediately skeptical of the concept with Norah O'Donnell on "Healthful."

item.title: Nashville airport one step closer to being renamed for Dolly Parton
item.description: The Metro Nashville Airport Authority board voted 6-0 on Friday to begin the process of changing the name and said a final name has not been chosen.

item.title: 25 years after 9/11 attacks, America reflects and remembers
item.description: Four former presidents were at the World Trade Center memorial site for 9/11 commemorations, while President Trump spoke at the Pentagon.

item.title: CIA declassifies dozens of never-before-seen 9/11 documents
item.description: The CIA released 71 reports from the months and years leading up to 9/11, providing a new look at what the spy agency told two presidents before the deadly strikes.

item.title: CBS News correspondent recounts being at Pentagon on 9/11
item.description: Longtime CBS News national security correspondent David Martin arrived at the Pentagon on Sept. 11, 2001, around 10 minutes after a plane crashed into the building. Martin joins to reflect on that day 25 years later.

item.title: Joe diGenova resigns from DOJ after overseeing "grand conspiracy" probe
item.description: Joe diGenova, the prosecutor who was tapped by Attorney General Todd Blanche to supervise the "grand conspiracy" investigation targeting Obama- and Biden-era officials, told CBS News he has resigned.

item.title: How lower-paid workers are getting their biggest pay raise in years
item.description: Some workers are seeing stronger wage growth by switching jobs, while others are "job-hugging" because of AI, research shows.

item.title: Record-setting cyclospora outbreak is over, U.S. health officials say
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said there is no longer a risk of people getting sick with cyclosporiasis from this outbreak and is confident that all related iceberg lettuce is off the market.

item.title: Why did my credit card company stop trying to collect my unpaid balance?
item.description: The calls from your credit card issuer may have stopped, but that silence may not mean what you think it does.

item.title: Anthropic says scientists used AI for possible biological weapons development
item.description: Anthropic said it blocked scientists who used its Claude AI models "in ways that could support biological weapons development."
